title: Refactor routing policy pipeline to 'safeguard' mode with typed config validation and staged rollout
creator: Aisha Nair
description: This ticket refactors the routing policy pipeline to a new 'safeguard' mode: authoritative typed validation, deterministic rule ordering, and an opt-in staged rollout. Goal is to reduce misrouted requests (region/tier/fallback), enable safer config migrations, and provide observability for policy regressions.
background: Our current DSL for routing rules mixes permissive schema checks with runtime heuristics. We have seen two classes of incidents: (1) ambiguous region selectors causing cross-region fallbacks under load, and (2) silent incompatibilities between policy authoring and executor (e.g., tier aliasing). Existing schema checks are ad-hoc and cannot express rule-level constraints like "if tier=dedicated then model must be pinned". The platform needs a typed, expressive validation layer plus a controlled rollout path so customers can author v2 policies without risking production impact.
proposal: Introduce a typed policy AST + JSON-schema-backed config surface, implement a 'safeguard' validator that enforces: (a) canonical region sets, (b) explicit tier-to-model contracts, (c) fallback variant compatibility matrix, and (d) deterministic evaluation order. Ship a policy simulation harness and CLI linter. Add a feature flag policy_v2_enabled per-tenant for staged rollout and a 'shadow-evaluate' mode that records telemetry without affecting routing. Migration will include automatic fixups for common anti-patterns and a manual review step for customer-visible changes.
acceptance_criteria: New validator rejects ambiguous region selectors with a clear error code and remediation hint
Policy simulation harness can re-run 10k historical requests offline and report any route diffs between v1 and v2
Feature flag per-tenant that supports shadow-evaluation for 24/7 without changing live routing
Automated CI lint step that fails on policy repo PRs if typed-schema violations are present
Dashboard shows policy-level metrics: rejections, shadow_diffs, fallback_rate, per-region routing latency
Performance: validator adds <1ms median overhead to admission path when cached; cold-validate still under 50ms
design_notes: We will represent policies as a small typed AST (protobuf or typed TS runtime). The AST will capture selectors (region sets, labels), routing decisions (tier, model variant, weight), and constraints (pinning, compatibility flags). Validation will run in two stages: schema validation (JSON Schema) and contract validation (typed rules). To avoid large deploy churn, runtime will accept both v1 permissive and v2 strict policies for a transitional period. The evaluator will be deterministic: stable sort by explicit priority then by creation timestamp.
technical_approach: 1) Define canonical enums for regions and tiers and add them to model catalog metadata. 2) Implement JSON Schema v7 for surface-level checks and a typed contract layer for inter-field constraints. 3) Build a validator library in Rust (for runtime) with a Thin Node module for editor integration. 4) Add shadow-eval hook in routing dispatcher that computes both v1 and v2 decisions and emits delta metrics. 5) Add a CLI 'policy-lint' backed by the same typed validator and integrate into CI. 6) Provide migration tooling that emits suggested fixes and a one-click GitHub PR template.
tradeoffs:
- Tightening validation increases authoring friction; mitigated by clear error hints and autofix suggestions.
- Implementing validator in Rust improves performance but increases infra knowledge for contributors (we'll provide a Node thin-wrapper).
- Shadow-eval doubles CPU in dispatcher for sampled traffic; we'll start at 1% sample and scale after baseline checks.
implementation_steps: Write canonical enumerations for regions and tiers and add to design doc (CONFLUENCE: /docs/routing/canonical-sets)
Define JSON Schema and typed AST for policy v2 and check in to policy-specs repo
Implement Rust validator library (crates/policy_validator) with Node shim
Build policy-lint CLI and integrate into policy-authoring GitHub org
Add dispatcher shadow hook and metric emission (routing.policy.shadow_diffs_count)
Create migration CLI to auto-propose fixes and open PRs with suggested policy edits
Run 10k historical request simulation and produce report; iterate on false positives
Enable per-tenant feature flag UI and rollout plan for opt-in customers
migration_plan: Phase 0: Spec stabilization and design review (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Validator + CLI and internal policy-lint integration. Early adopters invited (1 week)
Phase 2: Start shadow-eval at 1% globally, collect diffs, triage high-severity mismatches (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Offer automated fixups for low-risk changes and send PRs to customers who opted in (1 week)
Phase 4: Allow customers to opt-in to strict enforcement after 2 weeks of clean shadow results; default remains permissive for 8 weeks
Rollback: Feature flag off returns to v1 behavior. Migration scripts will preserve original policy files under .migrations/ for audit
qa_checks: Unit tests for schema + contract layers with >95% coverage
Integration test: simulate 10k requests comparing v1 and v2 outputs with seedable RNG
Perf test: cold and cached validator latency under 200ms (cold) and <1ms (cached)
Chaos test: enable with node failover to ensure shadow-eval does not affect routing during partial outages
Security: review KMS usage if policies are stored encrypted and audit logging is preserved
